counterexample_hunt_zalamtu.status: CONFIRMED — none is a first-person singular 'I wronged myself'; 'exactly 2 speakers' is airtight

speakers.27:44: قَالَتْ رَبِّ إِنِّى ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِى وَأَسْلَمْتُ مَعَ سُلَيْمَـٰنَ — the Queen (fem. verb qalat), submitting with Sulayman. CONFIRMED
speakers.28:16: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِى فَٱغْفِرْ لِى — Musa; 28:15 = فَوَكَزَهُۥ مُوسَىٰ فَقَضَىٰ عَلَيْهِ (the killing). CONFIRMED

distinguishing_verses.7:23: قَالَا رَبَّنَا ظَلَمْنَآ أَنفُسَنَا — dual (Adam + wife). Correctly excluded.
distinguishing_verses.21:87: إِنِّى كُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ — Yunus, different phrase. Correctly excluded.

checks.pagan_grounding: 27:24 وَجَدتُّهَا وَقَوْمَهَا يَسْجُدُونَ لِلشَّمْسِ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ — sun-worship, Quran-grounded (not hadith).
checks.quran_only: Payoff rests entirely on 27:44, 28:16, 27:24, 28:15 — no hadith dependency.
checks.overlap: Published corpus has zulm-al-nafs (concept) and 3 Bilqis pieces + many Musa pieces, but none makes this phrase-exact speaker-pairing. Adjacent, not duplicate.

soft_spots: Name 'Bilqis' is extra-Quranic (tafsir tradition), not in the Quran. Thesis body correctly says 'Queen of Sheba'; the exhibit uses 'Bilqis'. Page should say 'Queen of Sheba' or flag the name as traditional.

'Pagan Queen' is Quran-grounded via 27:24 (sun-worship) but at the moment of the utterance she is mid-submission ('wa aslamtu ma'a Sulayman'). Frame it as her prior identity, not her state at the confession.

Historical/narrative time reverses mushaf order (Musa's killing predates Sulayman's era by centuries). Keep framing scoped to 'in mushaf order' as written; do not imply the Queen's confession is historically first.
notes: All counts re-derived independently. Full phrase and 2-word core each appear in exactly 2 verses (27:44, 28:16); the three other 'ظلمت' verses are 2nd/3rd-person and not counterexamples. Speakers, killing context (28:15), pagan context (27:24), distinguishing verses (7:23, 21:87), and mushaf order all verified. Note: textSimple normalizes نفسى -> نفسي; using textSimple (as the exhibit prescribes) is the correct scope. No load-bearing failure. SURVIVES.
